audit.why: Tahm Kench's stun-stack poke and Devour deny the early lane through level 5 per packet.levelChart; Monsoon hard-countering Abyssal Dive at 6 and outright winning the disengage war vs his slow kit flips it to Janna, matching content win[4-6]=Janna.
Level-6 Monsoon-vs-Abyssal-Dive swing and first-item peel-breaks-his-Q-setup spikes are already correctly recorded in spikes[].

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side carry the placeholder 'Skill' while the full-layer .why text is written as if Janna wins every stage ('your chip is real and your disengage is law'), but content win[0-3]=Tahm Kench, win[4-6]=Janna, matching packet.levelChart exactly.
audit.why: THE CHART RULE requires side to agree with win[N]; since the why-text also argued the wrong side for the first four rows, both needed rewriting together. win[] itself needed no edit.
audit.corrected: Set phases[0-3].side to Tahm Kench with why rewritten from content whys[0-3] (stun-poke, three-stack all-in threat, Devour denying the pick, sustained poke), and phases[4-6].side to Janna with why tightened around content whys[4-6] (Monsoon vs Abyssal Dive, peel breaking Q setup, disengage war vs his immobile kit).

edits.before: Auto-harass with Tailwind and hold Q — your chip is real and your disengage is law.
edits.after: Tahm's Tongue Lash stun-poke and Thick Skin shield out-trade your Zephyr at level 1.

edits.before: W-poke the contacts; the tornado threat already taxes their engage plans.
edits.after: His three-stack stun threat at level 2 lets him win any all-in you start.

edits.before: Full kit: shield the trades, slow the answers, and break the first real engage with Q.
edits.after: His level 3 Devour denies any collapse you try to set on his ADC — it just eats the pick.

edits.before: Chip and shield the margins — every broken engage is a won trade your carry banks.
edits.after: Through 4-5 his sustained Q poke and Thick Skin regen keep the early lane in his favor.

edits.before: Monsoon online — dives on your duo now end in a healing field they paid for.
edits.after: At 6 Monsoon hard-counters Abyssal Dive outright, swinging the lane hard to you.

edits.before: First item: shields grow and the disengage toolkit compounds.
edits.after: First-item peel breaks his Q setup and slows his engage cold.

edits.before: Late Janna erases engages: tornado the dive, monsoon the collapse, shield the carry through the rest.
edits.after: Late, your disengage war and Zephyr slow leave his slow, immobile kit completely answerless.

edits.before: Auto the carry, W the support, shield the answer — chip trades the wind referees.
edits.after: Devour needs 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste before he can eat your carry — shield the marked ally before the third Tongue Lash lands.

edits.before: Burning Q on poke and meeting the real engage with a shrug — the tornado is the matchup.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive reaches 1000-1200 range and resets on hit — trading inside that threat range just feeds him a free dive-in.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His re-engage and his escape — all-in only while it is down. Read it before every duo step-up. - Your Q Howling Gale answers exactly one disaster per cooldown. - Spend the R on swing moments only.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive (W) is down 21s at rank 1, 17s maxed — that whiff is your punish window. - Tongue Lash refreshes every 7s early, so his stun stacks build fast; don't facetank three hits. - Devour has no cooldown of its own — three Q stacks is the real timer.

notes: All seven phases[N].side had been left as the literal placeholder 'Skill' while every full-layer .why argued Janna was winning, contradicting content win[0-3]=Tahm Kench/win[4-6]=Janna (already matching packet.levelChart). Synced side and rewrote whys 0-3 to Tahm's favor and 4-6 to Janna's, grounded in content whys[]/spikes[] and real ability names — no win[] edit needed. Resolved the packet defect (no cooldown-sequencing advice) by putting real numbers into breakdown.cooldowns (Abyssal Dive 21/17s, Tongue Lash 7s).
